paragraphs: Shakshuka belongs to the cooking traditions of the Maghreb—the North African region that includes Tunisia, Libya, Algeria, and Morocco. What holds the family together is the pan: vegetables and spices cooked into a concentrated sauce, then eggs set directly in it.

North African Jewish communities helped carry shakshuka into Israel, where it became an everyday café and home dish as well as a link to the food of Libya and Tunisia. Kwilt's version stays close to that practical form: cumin, paprika, pepper, and tomato cooked until thick enough to hold the eggs, with bread nearby for the sauce and soft yolks.
